subject: How to do a step-by-step plot from base R plot to ggplot2?

messages.author: 1064bc72b28574af
messages.subject: How to do a step-by-step plot from base R plot to ggplot2?
parts:
Dear ggplot2,

I have implemented the following plot R, I would like know how I can do it in ggplot2.

x <- rnorm(10)
y <- rnorm(10)
df1 <- cbind(x, y)

plot(-2:2, -2:2, type = "n")
for(i in 1:10){
  points(df1[i, 1], df1[i, 2], pch = 20)
  if(i!=1){
  lines(df1[(i-1):i,])
    }
}

Basically, I plot a point at step t, and connect it with next point at step t+1.

Should I do,
(1) ggplot() + geom_point(); OR
(2) geom_path()


Thank you very much!

Mike

messages.author: 74428f180627b7d7
messages.subject: Re: How to do a step-by-step plot from base R plot to ggplot2?
parts:
ggplot deals in dataframes ideally, and `geom_path` will plot in the 'original order' of the data. Assuming your data is ordered the way you want it plotted, it's simply

df2 <- as.data.frame(df1)


ggplot(data = df2, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_path(aes(group = 1)) +
  geom_point() +
  theme_bw()


if's it's not so ordered, refer to this question: http://stackoverflow.com/questions/19020532/ggplot2-line-plot-order

Olivia
